title.en: Atomic-hydrogen elastic cross section (momentum transfer and viscosity)
title.zh: 原子氢弹性动量转移截面

summary: H-on-H elastic cross section in m^2 as a function of collision energy in eV: a five-coefficient momentum-transfer logarithmic polynomial by default, with a distinct five-coefficient viscosity fit under viscosity=True. Both branches use the clipped [0.03, 1.01e4] eV domain. Negative energies are rejected and the branch selector must be a 0-d scalar.

capability: H-on-H momentum-transfer or viscosity elastic cross section in m^2 from collision energy in eV.
operation: Evaluate the H-on-H elastic cross section
collision energies and branch selector -> cross section per energy
discovery.model: Two independent empirical five-coefficient fits (momentum transfer by default, viscosity under viscosity=True); no external-data interpolation and no rate integration.
discovery.geometry: None; scalar material function of collision energy with no spatial axis (coordinate: collision energy in eV; output in m^2).
discovery.boundary: Energies must be finite and nonnegative; values outside the fit range clip to the endpoints; the selector must be a zero-dimensional scalar; both fits are strictly positive and finite on their clipped domains.

identity.relation: the H-on-H elastic cross section (momentum-transfer or viscosity fit) as a function of collision energy
identity.direction: collision energies and branch selector -> cross section per energy
identity.definition: Energies are clipped to [0.03, 1.01e4] eV and the cross section is exp(polyval(log(E_clipped), a)) * 1e-4 m^2 with the five coefficients of the selected branch (momentum transfer by default, viscosity under truthy selector). Endpoint values repeat outside the clipped range.
identity.model: two independent empirical cross-section fits; no interpolation of external data and no rate integration
identity.geometry: none; a scalar material function of collision energy
identity.coordinates: collision energy in eV; output cross section in m^2
identity.boundary: energies must be finite and nonnegative; in-domain values outside the fit range clip to the range endpoints; the selector must be a zero-dimensional scalar; both fits are strictly positive and finite on their clipped domains
assumptions: The two coefficient sets are the declared fit values, evaluated with the declared expressions; they are not re-derived from any external reference.
The two branches are different fits (momentum transfer vs viscosity cross sections), not equivalent parameterizations; selecting one is a caller decision.
Endpoint clipping is the declared behavior and is kept.
No external physical cross-section reference is bound; this residual stays open.

inputs.name: energy_ev
inputs.description: Collision energies at which the cross section is evaluated.
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative. Values above or below the fit range are clipped to the range endpoints.

inputs.name: viscosity
inputs.description: Branch selector: the viscosity fit when truthy, otherwise the momentum-transfer fit.
inputs.constraints: A zero-dimensional scalar interpreted as its truth value; higher-rank arrays are rejected.

outputs.name: cross_section_m2
outputs.description: Elastic cross section of the selected branch, one value per energy.
outputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive for every accepted input.

preconditions: The caller accepts the clipping convention: energies outside the fit range silently return the endpoint value.
The caller chooses the branch; the two fits are different quantities.
supported: H-on-H elastic momentum-transfer and viscosity cross sections on either fit within (or clamped to) its declared energy range.
Scalar and array evaluation of any shape, including zero-dimensional inputs.
Rejecting negative energies and higher-rank selectors.
excluded: Maxwellian averaging of this cross section: use scirel.collisions.maxwellian-relative-speed-rate-average, which accepts this callable as its cross_section_m2 port.
Charge-exchange or ionization channels: different relations, provided by sibling assets.
Elastic cross sections for other species pairs: separate assets, not variants of this relation.
A cross-section model validated against an external atomic-physics reference; none is bound.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError naming energy_ev for non-real, non-finite or negative energy inputs, or naming viscosity when that selector is not a zero-dimensional scalar.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Not reachable on the declared domain: both fits are evaluated only on their clipped positive range. No iteration, no state and no partial results.

example.description: Evaluate both branches, confirm the endpoint clipping, and confirm the negative-energy and array-selector rejections.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.collisions import evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_elastic_cross_section

energy = np.array([0.03, 1.0, 10.0, 100.0, 1.0e3, 1.01e4])
momentum = evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_elastic_cross_section(energy)
viscosity = evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_elastic_cross_section(energy, viscosity=True)
assert momentum.shape == energy.shape
assert np.all(np.isfinite(momentum)) and np.all(momentum > 0.0)
assert not np.allclose(momentum, viscosity, rtol=1e-12, atol=0.0)
clipped = evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_elastic_cross_section(np.array([0.01, 0.03, 2.0e4, 1.01e4]))
assert clipped[0] == clipped[1] and clipped[-1] == clipped[-2]
try:
    evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_elastic_cross_section(np.array([1.0, -0.5]))
except ValueError as error:
    assert 'nonnegative' in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError('a negative energy must be rejected')
try:
    evaluate_atomic_hydrogen_elastic_cross_section(energy, viscosity=np.ones((2, 2)))
except ValueError as error:
    assert 'viscosity' in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError('an array selector must be rejected')
example.expected: Finite strictly positive cross sections in m^2 on both branches, disagreeing with each other; endpoint repetition outside the clipped range; ValueError naming nonnegativity for a negative energy and naming viscosity for an array selector.

scope: That both branches equal independent evaluations of their coefficient sets on the clipped domain to a relative tolerance of 1e-15, and that the two branches disagree.
The endpoint clipping: values below and above the fit range repeat the endpoint values exactly.

The input contract: non-finite and negative energies rejected; higher-rank selectors rejected with a message naming viscosity. Both rejections are documented repairs; the selector repair replaces silent 0-d/size-1 acceptance and a generic NumPy ambiguity failure with a named 0-d-scalar requirement.

Exact bit-level agreement of both branches with an independent implementation of the same fit expressions, together with rejection witnesses (a negative energy raises ValueError, and a single-element array selector is rejected); the comparison is enabled only by an external implementation root and is not part of the default test run.
The composition contract: this callable serves directly as the cross_section_m2 port of scirel.collisions.maxwellian-relative-speed-rate-average and yields finite positive rate coefficients.
verification.evidence_ceiling: An independent evaluation of the fit expressions covers every branch, clipping boundary and SI conversion; a NumPy-only installation passed scalar independent evaluation across 56 energies per branch, and all 62 fit/input tests passed with their original assertions and tolerances. This qualifies the stated empirical expression, not new experimental accuracy. No external experimental cross-section validation is bound, and redistribution permission remains separate.
known_limitations: The integrated input check rejects complex, boolean and numeric-string energies before float conversion; no coercion is performed. Valid real-input fit arithmetic is unchanged.
Neither branch is validated against an external atomic-physics reference; no external validation gap is closed here.
Energies outside the fit range silently return the endpoint value; this is the declared clipping convention, not an error.
The two branches are different quantities, not equivalent forms; selecting the wrong one is a scientific error no runtime check can detect.
The negative-energy rejection is an explicit precondition of this contract: a negative energy raises ValueError rather than returning the clipped endpoint.
The optional cross-implementation comparison runs only in an environment that supplies an external implementation root; it is skipped otherwise and covers only the compared grids.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.
